newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hysan wakes up market with big purchase.
newsitem.headline: Hysan wakes up market with big purchase.

text.p: Hysan Development Ltd's purchase of a major Hong Kong property at a price well above recent market rates offers a bullish new benchmark for the core Central district market, analysts said on Friday.
"This (HK$17,000 per sq ft) is definitely the top end of the market," said Margaret Brooke, partner at chartered surveyors and property consultants Brooke Hillier Parker.

Chinese Estates Holdings Ltd said on Friday it had agreed to sell its 34-storey Entertainment Building in Central to Hysan for HK$3.64 billion. The price is equal to about HK$17,000 per sq ft for the 211,000 sq ft building.
The building, located in the heart of the prime Central business and commercial district on Hong Kong island, has a six-floor retail podium and 28 floors of office space.
While bullish for the overall office property market, the high price carries some negatives for Hysan.
"We believe that the current letting price for (office) space in the building is HK$50 per sq ft to HK$52 per sq ft. This gives a (gross) yield of around three percent to four percent," said Brooke.

Assuming Hysan's lending costs are some measure above the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate (HIBOR) but less than prime, currently 8.5 percent, the company is still looking at negative carrying costs or a negative yield during the early period until rental rates rise, analysts said.
Despite that large negative, the transaction sounds a wake-up call to an office property market that has been sluggish since tumbling off its early 1994 peak, analysts said.

"Hysan is a local player and currently the only major developer offering Grade A office space on Hong Kong island," said Euan Weir, investment analyst at Merrill Lynch. "They should know the market demand situation pretty well."
Weir added Hysan is paying a premium for the building because it carries a measure of status -- it is a trophy building and the company was able to buy the entire property.
"Still, it is a pretty punchy call on the property market," he said
Some analysts see the purchase as a signpost of the upturn in capital values of prime Hong Kong real estate.
"I think the price is a fair one," said Adrian Ngan, director at Peregrine Securities.
